newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks end lower in lacklustre trade.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks end lower in lacklustre trade.

text.p: Jakarta stocks ended lower in lacklustre trade on Tuesday with local-led profit-taking focused on medium and small stocks, brokers said.

The Jakarta composite index was down 2.74 points, or 0.40 percent, at 689.77 points after hitting an intra-day high of 693.33 points. Decliners led advancers by 81 to 45 with 71 issues unchanged. Total turn-over was estimated at 298 billion rupiah.
Brokers said local investors dominated trading but mostly encashed recent sharp gains in counters which were subjects of rumours of stock splits, bonus issues and take-overs.
"Today's correction in the index was partly due to weak regional markets. Look at Hong Kong and Singapore, the index fell sharply," one broker with a Singapore-based firm said.
The combination of lack of support from regional markets and continued foreign selling in some blue chip stocks helped push down the local index, he said.
"I expected the market to continue in the correction phase on Wednesday as we haven't executed all selling orders in some blue chip counters today," he added.
Brokers said sentiment on Wednesday was likely to be mixed as no fresh leads were available in the market.
Blue chip tobacco firms Sampoerna and Gudang Garam and telecommunications firm Indosat were among the targets of sellers, brokers said.
Property firm Surya Semesta Internusa was the most active stock with 12.5 million shares changing hands, last traded at an unchanged price of 1,225 rupiah.
"Active buying on Surya was linked to old rumours that one local conglomerate or foreign firm will buy a stake in the firm," a local broker said.

Transportation firm Mitra Rajasa was also active on renewed market talk of a possible take-over by one of the largest diversified business groups in the country, brokers said. It rose 25 rupiah to 1,350 rupiah on about 11 million shares.
Garment maker Karwell was also subject to rumours of a possible link-up with a foreign firm. The share rose 100 rupiah to 1,100 rupiah on 9.4 million shares.

Second-liner tourism services firm Bayu Buana was a target of profit-takers after recent sharp gains, brokers said. Bayu fell 75 rupiah to 1,325 rupiah, with around nine million shares traded, brokers said.
